newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish parliament votes to liberalise abortion.
newsitem.headline: Polish parliament votes to liberalise abortion.

text.p: The lower house of Poland's parliament voted on Thursday to overthrow a Senate veto and pass a bill liberalising the country's tough anti-abortion law -- a change fervently opposed by the Roman Catholic Church.
Deputies voted by 228 to 195 with 16 abstentions in favour of the bill, which ex-communist President Aleksander Kwasniewski has promised to sign.

The bill allows women to end pregnancies before the 12th week if they faced financial or personal problems, but only after counselling and a period of reflection, and also provides for sex education in schools and cheaper contraception.

Under the existing law, passed in 1993 by a pro-Catholic government, abortions are now allowed only if a pregnancy threatens a woman's life or health, results from incest or rape, or when the foetus is irreparably damaged.

The Church, drawing on the authority of Polish-born Pope John Paul, organised a huge protest campaign against what it sees as a licence to kill unborn children, culminating in a march in Warsaw on Wednesday by more than 30,000 people.

The bill, first passed by the lower house in August, was vetoed by the Senate early this month. The reform was backed by the main ruling coalition party, the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and some opposition deputies, while much of the SLD's smaller Peasant party coalition partner sided with right-leaning opposition groups in opposing it.
